runtime.name: omp
runtime.configuration: Hardened conflicting-writers fixture with isolated:true on both task items, but a dotted-key overlay did not establish the required apply=false behavior.
runtime.permissionProfile: two isolated writable implementers with automatic patch application into a disposable parent checkout

assertions.evidence: Only repository-generated Skills and the native implementer role participated.
The complete throughput checkpoint preceded delegation.
All four baseline hashes matched the fixture.
The task call recorded isolated:true twice, but merge summaries and the parent diff proved patches were automatically applied despite the claimed apply=false boundary.
Each retained patch changed exactly one owned numeric line.
Both writers ran in distinct isolated workspaces and returned distinct patches.
Both original results completed without follow-up, retry, replacement, or horizontal communication.
The root read both retained patches and their single-line ownership.
The runtime had already integrated both patches before the root inspection boundary, so the root's later reset and replay could not make the original apply=false claim true.
After root replay, the combined verifier passed and the final file matched expected bytes.
The final report disclosed the apply mismatch, but the run had already proceeded under a false apply=false premise instead of choosing a safe fallback.

limitations: The failure isolated a harness-configuration boundary rather than a writer-content defect.
The passing rerun writes isolation settings through a disposable OMP agent directory and reads back enabled=true, apply=false, and maxConcurrency=2 before launch.
